properties.statement:
⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-15, HOURS AFTER FILING, BY MEASUREMENT. THE REPORTED HARM DOES NOT OCCUR. As filed, this said a 16-char baseline 'compares unequal to every full-width recompute' and would report PERMANENT FALSE DRIFT. That was checked against the running 0.31.0 build and is FALSE: register `sha256:626d0572034645bf`, then reconcile against the full 64-char digest of the same bytes, and `reconcile_artifacts` returns `unchanged: 1, findings: 0`. `checksums_agree` requires a real prefix relationship and honours exactly this case — BL-160, fixed 2026-08-01, after the same phantom-drift class had been reported 51 times on a clean tree. 

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, AND IT IS MUCH SMALLER: `set_artifact_checksums` accepts a digest SHORTER than its named algorithm without remarking on it, so a caller who truncates by accident gets a WEAKER BASELINE THAN THEY THINK (16 hex = 64 bits) and is not told. The observation in the report was correct — it was accepted with `applied: true` on three artifacts, and was noticed only because the reply echoed the node back with the full digest in `location` beside the short one. Only the CONSEQUENCE was overstated. 

⛔ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY VALIDATING LENGTH AT THE BOUNDARY. Short digests are a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED DIALECT: reflow2's own `tools/build_design_graph.py` writes `hexdigest()[:16]`, and `checksums_agree` states the rule out loud — 'No minimum length is imposed. A short baseline is a weak baseline, but its strength is decided when it is registered — the write side takes a 16-char digest without complaint, and a read side that then refused to honour it would be the same write/read disagreement all over again.' Refusing short digests on write would break that generator, invalidate every existing short baseline, and re-open the write/read split those two functions exist to close. 

RESIDUAL ASK, IF ANY: a remark rather than a refusal — the reply could say the accepted digest is shorter than the named algorithm's width, which is the same 'say what you did' principle the `revision` block landed on 2026-08-15 under. That is a nicety, not a defect, and it is recorded here at that weight. 

THE SECOND-ORDER LESSON, worth more than the item: a capable reporter measured the OBSERVATION correctly and inferred the CONSEQUENCE without testing it, then ranked it first of five. The report was read, ranked first here too, and only survived to the fix stage because the code comment contradicted it. Consumer reports are evidence about what happened, not about what it means. || SOURCE: reported by the dev_storyflow fleet 2026-08-15 on reflow2 0.31.0; refuted by measurement against the same build the same day.
